summary_texts: The inputs together are further from their entered values than you stated

The estimate is the fit this analysis makes with the inputs as you entered them, the same way it fits each sample. Its unstarred estimates match the fit at the entered inputs under Fit results to the digits shown. The headline there differs because it lets the inputs move within the uncertainties you stated; its Conditional column is the fit at the entered inputs. The other columns cover all 2048 samples.

* The data fix only a combination of I0, ID and IHD, not each one on its own: many different sets of their values draw the same curve. Each starred row is a marginal summary: it shows how that one value spread across the samples, not how precisely the data determine it, so even a spread of 0 ± 0 does not mean the value is well determined, and its estimate can differ widely from the fit under Fit results.

The data fit only with the inputs, taken together, further from their entered values than their stated uncertainties allow (q = 23.9, p < 0.001). The fit put the correction here: [Host]₀ −11.3 % (3.8 σ), Guest (titrant, whole series) +9.3 % (3.1 σ), Ka,dye +3.0 % (0.3 σ), [Dye]₀ +0.2 % (0.1 σ) — the data see only 2 combinations of these 4 inputs, so the correction landed where those combinations point. Check the values you entered for them. The interval assumes the shifts are real.
Fit with the inputs as entered — lack-of-fit F(9, 60) = 389, p ≤ 0.005, simulated from the fitted curve and the noise law, with any addition error you stated
Fit with the inputs free to move — lack-of-fit F(9, 60) = 1.3, p = 0.32, simulated from the fitted curve and the noise law, with any addition error you stated
Inputs, taken together: q = 23.9 across 2 directions the data inform, p < 0.001. Shifts: [Host]₀ −11.3 % (3.8 σ), Guest (titrant, whole series) +9.3 % (3.1 σ), Ka,dye +3.0 % (0.3 σ), [Dye]₀ +0.2 % (0.1 σ).
Input uncertainties used: Ka,dye σ 10 %, [Host]₀ σ 3 %, [Dye]₀ σ 3 %, Guest (titrant, whole series) σ 3 %.
